thread:
amy (support): Hey team — customer (AcmeHealth) reports 500s on our API when they enable JSON mode for structured outputs. They get `parse_error: invalid_json` in our client. Trace ID: trace_0a7b2c. Happening intermittently, started ~2h ago. Repro steps included below.

tom (oncall): Thanks. Can you paste the exact client error and one raw model response (redact PII)? Also which model/variant and schema version are they using? :eyes:

amy (support): Error snippet from our SDK: `Error: StructuredOutputParseError: invalid_json at parseOutput (structured_parser.js:112)`
Model: open-llm/gpt-like-v1 (quantized-4bit). Schema: `v2-order-schema`. Customer supplied example prompt and config. Raw model chunk (redacted):
```
{"order_id": "1234", "items": [ {"sku": "X-1", "qty": 2}, ], "total": 49.98
```
Note the extra trailing comma before the closing array. They say it used to be fine last week.

ben (ml-obs): That trailing comma explains the JSON parse failure. Could be model drift after a fine-tuning or prompt change. Do we have parse_error metric spikes? Check PromQL: `sum(increase(redwood_structured_parse_errors_total{schema=\"v2-order-schema\"}[15m])) by (model_variant)` — look for spikes around 2h ago. Also check per-customer failure rate in the dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/structured-output?range=1h

amy (support): I ran the PromQL, there's a +63 spike for `open-llm/gpt-like-v1-quant4`. Dashboard shows their failure rate jumped from 0.3% to 12% in the last 2 hours.

olivia (privacy): Heads up — don't paste full customer prompts or API keys here. Amy, before sharing logs further, redact any name/SSN/etc. We need to ensure logs in the ticket are redacted. Use our scrub tool: `tools/redact --ticket 4523`.

deply-bot: (automated) Alert: structured-output-parse-error-threshold breached for model open-llm/gpt-like-v1-quant4 — incident #INC-20260317-17 created.

tom (oncall): Next steps: 1) Get a raw model output for the failing request (redacted), 2) if it's a trailing comma / missing bracket, recommend customer set `json_mode: "lenient"` temporarily or wrap responses in a top-level object and parse forgivingly, 3) escalate to eng-ml for model prompt rollback or kernel config. Assigning to ben.

ben (ml-obs): On it. Quick check: could be a tokenizer change in the quantized runtime that affects punctuation. I'll look at the model's recent rollout and inference-runtime patches. Also add a tracing span check: `trace.trace_id = \"trace_0a7b2c\"` — fetch the full trace in Console -> Traces.

amy (support): Repro curl (redacted):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"open-llm/gpt-like-v1-quant4","json_mode":true,"schema":"v2-order-schema","prompt":"<customer prompt>"}'
```
Customer says toggling `json_mode: false` removes the failures but they need structured outputs.

olivia (privacy): Amy — confirm that the customer has a data processing agreement covering this data. If not, mask any PHI before we keep traces.

ben (ml-obs): Found a recent inference-runtime commit (runtimelib 1.22.4 -> 1.22.5) that touched punctuation postprocessing for quantized models. Rolling back the change to a canary and re-running tests. If that fixes it, we'll promote the rollback and patch.

tom (oncall): Temporary mitigation for support: 1) instruct customer to set `schema_tolerance: 'strip_trailing_commas'` in their call (we can accept that param server-side for 1 week), OR 2) add a pre-parse step to run `jq -R 'fromjson? // . | .'` style tolerant parse before handing to strict validator. Which is quicker?

amy (support): I shared both options with the customer and enabled `schema_tolerance` on their account for 24h. They confirmed structured outputs are back to normal.

ben (ml-obs): Canary rollback fixes the deterministic punctuation issue on our internal test-suite. I'll coordinate a safe patch and add a regression test focused on trailing commas and missing bracket cases. Also adding a metric `redwood_structured_parser_recoveries_total` for tolerance fallbacks.

olivia (privacy): Good. For the ticket notes: mark that we enabled per-customer tolerant parsing and redacted traces. Don't store customer prompt in plaintext in public dashboards.

tom (oncall): Closing loop: root cause — runtime postprocessing change caused punctuation drift for quantized variant; symptom — invalid JSON from model causing parse_error spikes; mitigation — per-customer tolerance + rollback canary; next action — patch + regression tests + dashboard alert tuned to model-variant spikes. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

amy (support): I'll update the support ticket and the customer. Leaving the incident open for the patch.

ben (ml-obs): Leaving a follow-up PR to add a CI eval that generates JSON outputs and runs our strict validator across variants.

olivia (privacy): I'll audit the retention of the redacted trace to ensure compliance.

(ended)
